decisions.reason: As a large incumbent in protective footwear, the firm is likely to keep a newly launched safety shoe line on the market because it is close to the core business and one year is usually too early to abandon such an option without clearer negative evidence.

A comfort insole is relatively low-cost to keep as an add-on option, but its only basic website mention and overlap with other insole launches make it somewhat more exposed to later portfolio pruning.

The supportive insole still looks worth keeping because uncertainty about demand is probably not fully resolved after one year, though its modest web prominence and similarity to adjacent insole products raise the chance of later withdrawal.

An ergonomic safety shoe series shown on its own page signals stronger commitment and perceived strategic value, so real-options logic points to keeping it while the firm learns more about market acceptance.

Firefighter and rescue boots fit the firm's technical footwear capabilities, but the niche market and only limited website prominence imply a moderate risk of withdrawal if early demand proves narrow.

Being shown on the home page suggests the moulded insole received above-average commercial attention, and because it is inexpensive to keep relative to a full footwear line the firm is likely to continue it for now.
